title: RÈGLEMENT 2026 — HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc (Internet Archive snapshot)
claims: For UTMB, CCC and TDS, personal assistance is tolerated only at designated aid stations, by one person, with no equipment other than a bag of at most 30 litres; medical assistance from a runner's own team is forbidden. For OCC, MCC and ETC no assistance is permitted anywhere on the course.
Pacing or being accompanied by a non-entrant is forbidden outside marked spectator areas and can be penalised per notification.

The organiser publishes a base mandatory-equipment list for all runners plus additional items that can be activated individually; activated items are communicated no later than 24 hours before the start, and all base plus activated items must be carried for the whole race.
Sealed bags that cannot be reopened and any packaging preventing an immediate check are forbidden; all mandatory equipment must be accessible and controllable at any time.
If poles are used, they must be carried from the start for the whole race; poles are not accepted in drop bags, and no disposable cutlery, cups or bowls are distributed at aid stations.
When a race starts in several waves, the maximum allowed time and cut-off times are calculated from the start of the last wave.

Penalties: missing a critical safety item is a disqualification; other missing equipment is 1 hour at CCC and 30 minutes at OCC; assistance outside authorised zones is 1 hour at CCC and 30 minutes at OCC; pacing is 15 minutes per notification at CCC and 10 minutes at OCC; starting before an assigned wave is 2 hours at CCC and 1 hour at OCC.
Each runner must hold individual accident insurance covering search and evacuation costs in France, Italy and Switzerland; the requirement is mandatory for the HOKA UTMB Mont-Blanc.
Deliberate littering is penalised 1 hour at CCC and 30 minutes at OCC.
Time penalties are served immediately on the spot, during which the runner must stop racing; the runner's race clock is not stopped.
